[TestGrid](https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-release-master-blocking#gce-cos-master-default&width=5&include-filter-by-regex=should.delete.a.collection.of.pods) currently show 7 failed tests.

Checking on ~30 successful test runs shows that;
- 12 seconds for the longest wait time for a pod to delete
- 16 seconds for the longest wait time for all pods to delete

Most of the [test failures (e.g. 1285144199905153026/build-log.txt)](https://storage.googleapis.com/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gci-gce/1285144199905153026/build-log.txt) are ending along the same lines of;

Any tips/thoughts on how to fix this e2e test would be appreciated. TIA

I've started running the test by itself in a loop in the background. This seems to be running the desired test
```
make test-e2e-node PARALLELISM=1 TEST_ARGS='--kubelet-flags=--fail-swap-on=false' FOCUS="Pods should delete a collection of pods" SKIP="\[Flaky\]|\[Serial\]" RUN_UNTIL_FAILURE=true
```
Up to 50+ runs locally without a failure.


From a limited look at the three most recent failing logs, it looks like the pod gets cleaned up a bit outside of the time limit.

I'm not sure if 1 minute is a valid period to wait for a delete or not. Docs mention something about "the default grace period for the specified type will be used." but I have no idea how to check what that is for a pod. Could it be `kubectl explain pod.spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds`? That says 30 seconds for me, which I'm not sure is set/enforced by client or server.

Things to try:
1. set GracePeriodSeconds to 0 for deletion options.
2. increase the amount of time to wait for deletion (not sure if this is a valid thought)
3. wait for the pods to be running? Looks to me the pods could be deleted before even being scheduled, as soon as they show up in etcd to be listable. I'd have to understand the pod lifecycle more in depth to know when a pod becomes listable, and what it means that it is.

from a reviewing the test: 
Add a By() after the "waiting for pods to be located" (What does located mean? I don't understand) and the call to delete so we are aware of that STEP during the running of the test.


Could this be related to other grace period trouble around now? Or is that only for static-pods?

Jumping in o try and help debug the failures for this test as well :nerd_face: 
So first off, the test we are looking at is called `[k8s.io] Pods should delete a collection of pods`.
Grep'ing k/k/test tells me where this test is implemented
```
$ grep -nr "should delete a collection of pods"
e2e/common/pods.go:835:	ginkgo.It("should delete a collection of pods", func() {
```
Which lands us in
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c2b7aa0353d509c07ce7c2c152af861fbc84c7f5/test/e2e/common/pods.go#L835

A good set of test logs to follow from (click on a red test run from testgrid) https://prow.k8s.io/view/gcs/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gci-gce/1285144199905153026

Then it creates some pods
```
I0720 09:39:09.070] STEP: Create set of pods
I0720 09:39:09.070] Jul 20 09:37:56.081: INFO: created test-pod-1
I0720 09:39:09.071] Jul 20 09:37:56.252: INFO: created test-pod-2
I0720 09:39:09.071] Jul 20 09:37:56.462: INFO: created test-pod-3
```
with the code here https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c2b7aa0353d509c07ce7c2c152af861fbc84c7f5/test/e2e/common/pods.go#L838


It waits for the pods to be present,
```
I0720 09:39:09.071] STEP: waiting for all 3 pods to be located
```
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c2b7aa0353d509c07ce7c2c152af861fbc84c7f5/test/e2e/common/pods.go#L858-L861

Which seems to succeed.
And then the pods are deleted.

The first step is a call to delete the collection
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c2b7aa0353d509c07ce7c2c152af861fbc84c7f5/test/e2e/common/pods.go#L863-L866
Which again, seems to succed but then we the test fails every now and then at the last step
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c2b7aa0353d509c07ce7c2c152af861fbc84c7f5/test/e2e/common/pods.go#L868-L871

The tests pods do seem to be deleted, slowly.
The deletion process starts with
```
I0720 09:39:09.071] Jul 20 09:37:58.137: INFO: Pod quantity 3 is different from expected quantity 0
I0720 09:39:09.072] Jul 20 09:37:59.236: INFO: Pod quantity 3 is different from expected quantity 0
I0720 09:39:09.072] Jul 20 09:38:00.353: INFO: Pod quantity 3 is different from expected quantity 0
I0720 09:39:09.072] Jul 20 09:38:01.270: INFO: Pod quantity 3 is different from expected quantity 0
I0720 09:39:09.072] Jul 20 09:38:02.244: INFO: Pod quantity 2 is different from expected quantity 0
```
so after some 4s, 1 pod is deleted.
A second pod is deleted within some 2 more seconds.
But then, the last pod hangs around for more than 50s.
This last bit leads to a timeout and causes the test to fail.

Since this kind of error is relatively infrequent ( 5 failures in the last 6 days), one possible route would be to increase the timeout when checking if a pod has been deleted
```go
// podRetryTimeout is set to 1 minute, so let's increase it.
err = wait.PollImmediate(podRetryPeriod, 2 * time.Minute, checkPodListQuantity(f, "type=Testing", 0))
```

Will continue checking for more info - to make sure the timeout is not hiding something else (i dont think its lightly but i havent spent much time with this test).

Went log surfing a little more and the only info about the test pods used for this e2e tests that is logged after the failure is
```
I0720 09:39:09.169] Jul 20 09:39:04.958: INFO: test-pod-3 started at 2020-07-20 09:37:56 +0000 UTC (0+1 container statuses recorded)
I0720 09:39:09.169] Jul 20 09:39:04.958: INFO: 	Container token-test ready: true, restart count 0
```
https://prow.k8s.io/view/gcs/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gci-gce/1285144199905153026#1:build-log.txt%3A33963

There isn't anything particularly weird with the pod so maybe it is one of those instances in which a pod just takes longer to be deleted.

# API Reference and feature documentation
* [Kubernetes API Reference Docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/kubernetes-api/)
* [Kubernetes API: v1.18 /deleteCoreV1CollectionNamespacedPod](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.18/#delete-collection-pods-v1-core)
* [client-go - Pod: DeleteCollection](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/master/kubernetes/typed/core/v1/pod.go)

# The mock test
## Test outline
1. Create a set of 3 Pods with a static label within a Namespace.
2. Confirm that all 3 Pods with the label in the Namespace are created.
3. Delete the set of Namespaced Pods with a label via DeleteCollection.
4. Confirm that all Pods with the label have been deleted.

## Test the functionality in Go
```go
package main

import (
  // "encoding/json"
  "fmt"
  "time"
  "flag"
  "os"
  v1 "k8s.io/api/core/v1"
  // "k8s.io/client-go/dynamic"
  // "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/runtime/schema"
  metav1 "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1"
  "k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes"
  // "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/types"
  "k8s.io/client-go/tools/clientcmd"
)

func main() {
  // uses the current context in kubeconfig
  kubeconfig := flag.String("kubeconfig", fmt.Sprintf("%v/%v/%v", os.Getenv("HOME"), ".kube", "config"), "(optional) absolute path to the kubeconfig file")
  flag.Parse()
  config, err := clientcmd.BuildConfigFromFlags("", *kubeconfig)
  if err != nil {
    fmt.Println(err)
    return
  }
  // make our work easier to find in the audit_event queries
  config.UserAgent = "live-test-writing"
  // creates the clientset
  ClientSet, _ := kubernetes.NewForConfig(config)

  // TEST BEGINS HERE

  // create a set of pod test names
  podTestNames := [3]string{"test-pod-nginx-1", "test-pod-nginx-2", "test-pod-nginx-3"}

  // create a set of test pods with a label in the default namespace
  for _, podTestName := range podTestNames {
    _, err = ClientSet.CoreV1().Pods("default").Create(&v1.Pod{
      ObjectMeta: metav1.ObjectMeta{
        Name: podTestName,
        Labels: map[string]string{
          "type": "Testing"},
      },
      Spec: v1.PodSpec{
        Containers: []v1.Container{{
          Image: "nginx",
          Name: "nginx",
        }},
        RestartPolicy: v1.RestartPolicyNever,
      }})

    if err != nil {
      fmt.Println("[error]", err)
      return
    }
    fmt.Println("[status] created", podTestName)
    time.Sleep(3 * time.Second)
  }

  // get a list of Pods with a label in the default namespace
  podsList, err := ClientSet.CoreV1().Pods("default").List(metav1.ListOptions{
    LabelSelector: "type=Testing"})

  // check that there are 3 pods found
  fmt.Println("[status] Found", len(podsList.Items), "pods")
  if len(podsList.Items) != 3 {
    fmt.Println("[error] Incorrect number of Pods found")
    return
  }

  // delete Collection of Pods for the label in the default namespace
  _  = ClientSet.CoreV1().Pods("default").DeleteCollection(&metav1.DeleteOptions{}, metav1.ListOptions{
         LabelSelector: "type=Testing"})
  fmt.Println("[status] DeleteCollection processed")

  // Give the cluster time to delete all pods
  time.Sleep(30 * time.Second)

  // get a list of Pods in the default namespace with the label
  podsList, err = ClientSet.CoreV1().Pods("default").List(metav1.ListOptions{
    LabelSelector: "type=Testing"})
  if err != nil {
    fmt.Println("[error]", err)
    return
  }

  // check that there are no pods found
  fmt.Println("[status] Found", len(podsList.Items), "pods")
  if len(podsList.Items) != 0 {
    fmt.Println("[error] Still found a Pod(s)")
    return
  }

  // TEST ENDS HERE

  fmt.Println("[status] complete")

}
```
